title: Releasing statistics in spreadsheets
source: UK Government Analysis Function (Analysis Function Central Team, ONS), Releasing statistics in spreadsheets, published 30 June 2021, read 2026-10-08.
note: Scope 'every' applies to any workbook and the app checks the scripted ones; scope 'statistics' applies to a published statistics table.

rules.text: Every data table is marked up as an Excel table with a header row.
Tables have meaningful names, a plain style and no filter buttons.
rules.source: Naming tables; Make the default table accessible

rules.text: No merged or split cells and no tables inside tables.
rules.source: Merged and split cells and nested tables

rules.text: No fully blank row or column inside a table.
rules.source: Blank rows and columns within tables

rules.text: One header row, and every column has its own unique text heading.
The same variable carries the same heading everywhere in the workbook.
Units go in round brackets after the heading.
One precision per column, thousands separated, a leading zero before a decimal point.
Totals sit at the edge of a table.
Avoid filters and freeze panes; if used, say so in column A above the table.
A cell with no data is blank for one explained reason or carries a bracketed shorthand such as [x]; never '..', '-' or 'NA'.
No superscripts or symbols as markers; write [note 1] and explain shorthand in column A.
Markers stay out of data cells, so a column of numbers holds numbers only.
Detailed notes go in a table on a sheet named Notes.
A code sits in its own labelled cell, apart from its name and the data.
Colour, shading or patterns are never the only way meaning is shown.
No vertical or diagonal text and no letter-spaced words.
No hidden rows or columns unless column A explains them.
Text of 10 point or more in a sans-serif face, in the automatic colour, without italics or underlining.
Text is left-aligned; figures and their headings are right-aligned.
No indents made with the indent tool and no leading or trailing spaces in cells or sheet names.
Periods are written out, such as Jan to Mar 2020, with full years and no dashes.
Link text says where it goes, never 'click here' or a bare long address.
Avoid images, logos and text boxes, and keep nothing important in headers or footers.
A complex workbook opens with a cover sheet and a table of contents.
rules.source: Cover sheet and table of contents

rules.text: Sheet names are unique and say what is on the sheet, and no sheet is blank.
Cell A1 says what the sheet holds and A2 describes it.
rules.source: Information in column A; Where to place titles

rules.text: A table starts in column A, with nothing below it.
One table per sheet, titled with the data, the period and the place.
With several tables on a sheet, A2 gives their number and each has its own title.
The cover gives the title, a summary, the source, the dates, the revision status and a contact, in column A.
Confidence bounds and significance go in their own labelled cells, in words rather than asterisks.
A published table carries no macros, and its formulas are replaced by their values.
Saved with the cursor in A1 on every sheet and the first sheet active.
The workbook's title and language are set in its properties.
File names are short, lowercase and joined by dashes, without draft, final or a version.
